# 1. Introduction 

The CIELAB colour profiles of images of two sediment cores sampled from Lake Hillier were used to investigate their relative depth alignments. Pearson cross-correlation of the cores’ L* profiles identified several candidate offsets, with the strongest peaks producing plausible alignments despite relatively weak correlation coefficients (typically around r = 0.3).

Repeated light and dark banding produced periodic patterns in the cross-correlation, likely explaining the presence of multiple competing peaks. Correlation peaks were also observed between core sections that are not expected to overlap stratigraphically. While these observations do not invalidate the method, they highlight the limitations of cross-correlation alone in establishing the correct alignment.

# 2. Data and Analysis

Images of the upper (A) and lower (B) parts of cores ML-24-03 and ML-24-04 where used to extract depth-aligned CIELAB profiles. The Sedivis software was used to crop these images, calibrate their depth scales and extract colour data by averaging the RGB pixel values across each row, then convert these values to the CIELAB colour space assuming a D65 reference white.

```{r load-images, include=FALSE}

# Loading the images
```

```{r load-data, include=FALSE}
load_data = function(folder, file) {
```

We note that the depth intervals differ between cores:
```{r depth-intervals, echo=FALSE}
list(
  "MI-24-03" = range(diff(core_3A$depth_mm)),
  "MI-24-04" = range(diff(core_4A$depth_mm))
)
```

We therefore resample all colour profiles to a common 0.5 mm interval before analysis.

```{r analysis-settings}
depth_step_mm = 0.5
max_offset_mm = 1000
```

```{r resample-depth, include=FALSE}

# Resampling all profiles to 0.5 mm depth intervals
resample = function(series, depth_step = depth_step_mm) {

  depth = seq(
    ceiling(min(series$depth_mm) / depth_step) * depth_step,
    floor(max(series$depth_mm) / depth_step) * depth_step,
    by = depth_step
  )

  series |>
    reframe(
      depth_mm = depth,
      across(
        -depth_mm,
        ~ approx(
          series$depth_mm,
          .x,
          xout = depth,
          ties = mean
        )$y
      )
    )
}

core_3A = resample(core_3A)
core_3B = resample(core_3B)

core_4A = resample(core_4A)
core_4B = resample(core_4B)
```

```{r pearson-cross-correlation, echo=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=6, fig.align='center'}

pairs = list(
  c("core_3A", "core_4A"),
  c("core_3A", "core_4B"),
  c("core_3B", "core_4A"),
  c("core_3B", "core_4B")
)

for (pair in pairs) {

  core_1 = get(pair[1])
  core_2 = get(pair[2])

  image_1 = get(sub("core_", "image_", pair[1]))
  image_2 = get(sub("core_", "image_", pair[2]))

  name_1 = sub("core_", "MI-24-0", pair[1])
  name_2 = sub("core_", "MI-24-0", pair[2])

  # Pearson cross-correlation

  result = ccf(
    core_1$L_star,
    core_2$L_star,
    lag.max = round(max_offset_mm / depth_step),
    plot = FALSE
  )

  best = which.max(result$acf)

  offset_mm = as.vector(result$lag)[best] * depth_step
  correlation = as.vector(result$acf)[best]

  cat(
    pair[1], "vs", pair[2],
    "| Pearson r =", round(correlation, 4),
    "| Lag =", round(offset_mm, 1), "mm\n"
  )

  # Cross-correlation plot

  ccf_df = data.frame(
    lag_mm = as.vector(result$lag) * depth_step_mm,
    correlation = as.vector(result$acf)
  )

  print(
    ggplot(ccf_df, aes(x = lag_mm, y = correlation)) +
      geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey70") +
      geom_segment(
        aes(xend = lag_mm, y = 0, yend = correlation),
        colour = "grey55",
        linewidth = 0.25
      ) +
      geom_vline(
        xintercept = offset_mm,
        colour = "steelblue",
        linewidth = 0.8
      ) +
      labs(
        title = paste(name_1, "vs", name_2),
        subtitle = sprintf(
          "Maximum Pearson r = %.3f  |  Lag = %.1f mm",
          correlation, offset_mm
        ),
        x = "Depth lag (mm)",
        y = "Pearson correlation (r)"
      ) +
      theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
      theme(
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10),
        plot.margin = margin(10, 15, 10, 10)
      )
  )

  # Aligned core images

  depth_1 = range(core_1$depth_mm)
  depth_2 = range(core_2$depth_mm) + offset_mm

  depth_min = min(depth_1, depth_2)
  depth_max = max(depth_1, depth_2)

  dimensions_1 = magick::image_info(image_1)
  dimensions_2 = magick::image_info(image_2)

  width_1 = diff(depth_1) *
    dimensions_1$width / dimensions_1$height

  width_2 = diff(depth_2) *
    dimensions_2$width / dimensions_2$height

  gap = max(width_1, width_2) * 0.3

  x1_min = 0
  x1_max = width_1

  x2_min = width_1 + gap
  x2_max = x2_min + width_2

  # Core image plot

  print(
    ggplot() +
      annotation_raster(
        as.raster(image_1),
        xmin = x1_min,
        xmax = x1_max,
        ymin = depth_1[1],
        ymax = depth_1[2],
        interpolate = TRUE
      ) +
      annotation_raster(
        as.raster(image_2),
        xmin = x2_min,
        xmax = x2_max,
        ymin = depth_2[1],
        ymax = depth_2[2],
        interpolate = TRUE
      ) +
      scale_x_continuous(
        breaks = NULL,
        limits = c(x1_min, x2_max),
        expand = expansion(mult = 0.05)
      ) +
      scale_y_reverse(
        limits = c(depth_min, depth_max),
        expand = expansion(mult = 0.02)
      ) +
      coord_fixed(ratio = 1) +
      labs(
        title = paste("Core alignment:", name_1, "and", name_2),
        subtitle = sprintf(
          "Offset = %.1f mm  |  Pearson r = %.3f",
          offset_mm, correlation
        ),
        x = NULL,
        y = "Depth (mm)"
      ) +
      annotate(
        "text",
        x = c(
          (x1_min + x1_max) / 2,
          (x2_min + x2_max) / 2
        ),
        y = depth_max + 0.04 * (depth_max - depth_min),
        label = c(name_1, name_2),
        size = 3
      ) +
      theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
      theme(
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10),
        axis.line.x = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 25, 10)
      )
  )
}
```


## Running with R^3 offset space

We first construct a three-dimensional search space of candidate offsets for cores MI-24-03B, MI-24-04A and MI-24-04B, keeping MI-24-03A fixed as the reference. Each offset ranges from (-500) to (500) mm in increments of (5) mm. Configurations in which the upper (A) and lower (B) sections of the same core overlap or occur out of sequence are excluded.

We then iterate through the remaining configurations, calculating the Pearson correlation coefficient, (r), using the L* values at shared depths. In future, this second step could benefit from parallel processing, as the individual correlation calculations are independent.
```{r}
# Search settings (mm)
max_gap = 200
min_overlap_fraction = 0.5
offset_step = 5

# Core depth ranges
range_3A = range(core_3A$depth_mm)
range_3B = range(core_3B$depth_mm)
range_4A = range(core_4A$depth_mm)
range_4B = range(core_4B$depth_mm)

# Core lengths
length_3A = diff(range_3A)
length_3B = diff(range_3B)
length_4A = diff(range_4A)
length_4B = diff(range_4B)

# Reference: top of 3A at depth 0
bottom_3A = length_3A

# Candidate gaps within each core
gap_values = seq(0, max_gap, by = offset_step)

# Candidate positions for 3B
positions_3B = bottom_3A + gap_values

# Candidate positions for 4A
# Allow 4A to move above or below 3A, subject to minimum overlap
total_3 = length_3A + length_3B
total_4 = length_4A + length_4B

min_overlap = min_overlap_fraction * min(total_3, total_4)

positions_4A = seq(
  -total_4 - max_gap,
  total_3 + max_gap,
  by = offset_step
)

# Full search space: 3B position, 4A position, and gap within core 4
offsets = expand.grid(
  position_3B = positions_3B,
  position_4A = positions_4A,
  gap_4 = gap_values
)

# Position of 4B relative to 4A
offsets$position_4B =
  offsets$position_4A + length_4A + offsets$gap_4

# Calculate overlap between two intervals
interval_overlap = function(a_start, a_end, b_start, b_end) {
  pmax(0, pmin(a_end, b_end) - pmax(a_start, b_start))
}

# Total overlap between the two cores
# Count only sediment-bearing intervals, not gaps
offsets$overlap =
  interval_overlap(
    0, length_3A,
    offsets$position_4A,
    offsets$position_4A + length_4A
  ) +
  interval_overlap(
    0, length_3A,
    offsets$position_4B,
    offsets$position_4B + length_4B
  ) +
  interval_overlap(
    offsets$position_3B,
    offsets$position_3B + length_3B,
    offsets$position_4A,
    offsets$position_4A + length_4A
  ) +
  interval_overlap(
    offsets$position_3B,
    offsets$position_3B + length_3B,
    offsets$position_4B,
    offsets$position_4B + length_4B
  )

# Enforce minimum overlap
offsets = subset(
  offsets,
  overlap >= min_overlap
)

# Convert positions to offsets for the existing correlation function
offsets$offset_3B =
  offsets$position_3B + range_3A[1] - range_3B[1]

offsets$offset_4A =
  offsets$position_4A + range_3A[1] - range_4A[1]

offsets$offset_4B =
  offsets$position_4B + range_3A[1] - range_4B[1]

# Keep the columns expected by calculate_correlations()
offsets = offsets[, c(
  "offset_3B",
  "offset_4A",
  "offset_4B"
)]

cat(
  "Possible configurations:",
  format(nrow(offsets), big.mark = ","),
  "\n"
)
```

Calculating the r values for each config. 
```{r}

plan(multisession, workers = 4)
# plan(multisession, workers = max(1, parallel::detectCores() - 1))
plan()
```

```{r}
calculate_correlations = function(offsets) {

  evaluate = function(offset_3B, offset_4A, offset_4B) {

    core_3 = rbind(
      data.frame(
        depth = core_3A$depth_mm,
        L_star = core_3A$L_star
      ),
      data.frame(
        depth = core_3B$depth_mm + offset_3B,
        L_star = core_3B$L_star
      )
    )

    core_4 = rbind(
      data.frame(
        depth = core_4A$depth_mm + offset_4A,
        L_star = core_4A$L_star
      ),
      data.frame(
        depth = core_4B$depth_mm + offset_4B,
        L_star = core_4B$L_star
      )
    )

    aligned = merge(
      core_3,
      core_4,
      by = "depth",
      suffixes = c("_3", "_4")
    )

    aligned = aligned[complete.cases(aligned), ]

    if (nrow(aligned) < 3) {
      return(NA_real_)
    }

    cor(
      aligned$L_star_3,
      aligned$L_star_4,
      method = "pearson"
    )
  }

  # Split into chunks to reduce parallel overhead
  chunk_size = 10000
  chunks = split(
    seq_len(nrow(offsets)),
    ceiling(seq_len(nrow(offsets)) / chunk_size)
  )

  progressr::handlers("txtprogressbar")

  correlations = progressr::with_progress({
    p = progressr::progressor(steps = length(chunks))

    future.apply::future_lapply(
      chunks,
      function(idx) {

        values = mapply(
          evaluate,
          offsets$offset_3B[idx],
          offsets$offset_4A[idx],
          offsets$offset_4B[idx]
        )

        p()
        values
      },
      future.seed = FALSE
    )
  })

  offsets$pearson_r = unlist(correlations, use.names = FALSE)

  offsets
}

results = calculate_correlations(offsets)

plan(sequential)


```



```{r}
best = results[which.max(results$pearson_r), ]
print(best)
```


```{r}
results <- results %>%
  arrange(desc(pearson_r))

print(results)


high_values <- results %>%
  filter(pearson_r > 0.2)

print(length(high_values))
```


Visualising the results

```{r}
# Core images at the global maximum

cores = list(
  list(image = image_3A, data = core_3A, offset = 0, side = 1, name = "MI-24-03A"),
  list(image = image_3B, data = core_3B, offset = best$offset_3B, side = 1, name = "MI-24-03B"),
  list(image = image_4A, data = core_4A, offset = best$offset_4A, side = 2, name = "MI-24-04A"),
  list(image = image_4B, data = core_4B, offset = best$offset_4B, side = 2, name = "MI-24-04B")
)

# Calculate image positions, preserving aspect ratios

for (i in seq_along(cores)) {

  core = cores[[i]]

  dimensions = magick::image_info(core$image)

  core$ymin = min(core$data$depth_mm) + core$offset
  core$ymax = max(core$data$depth_mm) + core$offset

  core$width = (core$ymax - core$ymin) *
    dimensions$width / dimensions$height

  cores[[i]] = core
}

# Horizontal layout

width_3 = max(vapply(cores[1:2], function(x) x$width, numeric(1)))
width_4 = max(vapply(cores[3:4], function(x) x$width, numeric(1)))

gap = max(width_3, width_4) * 0.5

for (i in seq_along(cores)) {

  core = cores[[i]]

  core$xmin = if (core$side == 1) {
    (width_3 - core$width) / 2
  } else {
    width_3 + gap + (width_4 - core$width) / 2
  }

  core$xmax = core$xmin + core$width

  cores[[i]] = core
}

# Plot limits

depth_min = min(vapply(cores, function(x) x$ymin, numeric(1)))
depth_max = max(vapply(cores, function(x) x$ymax, numeric(1)))

x_min = 0
x_max = width_3 + gap + width_4

# Build plot

p = ggplot()

for (core in cores) {

  p = p +
    annotation_raster(
      as.raster(core$image),
      xmin = core$xmin,
      xmax = core$xmax,
      ymin = core$ymax,
      ymax = core$ymin,
      interpolate = TRUE
    )
}

# Labels above each core column

label_positions = data.frame(
  x = c(width_3 / 2, width_3 + gap + width_4 / 2),
  y = depth_min,
  label = c("MI-24-03", "MI-24-04")
)

p = p +
  geom_text(
    data = label_positions,
    aes(x = x, y = y, label = label),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    vjust = 1.5,
    fontface = "bold",
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(x_min, x_max),
    breaks = NULL,
    expand = expansion(mult = 0.1)
  ) +
  scale_y_reverse(
    limits = c(depth_max, depth_min),
    expand = expansion(mult = 0.04)
  ) +
  coord_fixed(
    ratio = 1,
    clip = "off"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Core Alignment — Global Maximum",
    subtitle = sprintf(
      "Pearson r = %.3f  |  3B = %+.0f mm  |  4A = %+.0f mm  |  4B = %+.0f mm",
      best$pearson_r,
      best$offset_3B,
      best$offset_4A,
      best$offset_4B
    ),
    x = NULL,
    y = "Depth relative to MI-24-03A (mm)"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.line.x = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
    plot.margin = margin(15, 15, 15, 15)
  )

# Save plot

ggsave(
  filename = "global_max_alignment.png",
  plot = p,
  width = 8,
  height = 12,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 200,
  device = "png",
  limitsize = FALSE
)
```
